# S19 — Interactive inbox: adj inbox -i

Add adj inbox -i: a line-mode walk through the open questions, oldest first, where the owner decides, rejects, withdraws or skips each one, with a rationale, without retyping IDs and option labels.

**Findings:** PROJECT.md Feature tiers (Later) · **Size:** M · **Tree:** cli

**2026-10-18** — C32: Use -i only (no long alias); --by requires -i. Actions d/t/r/w/s/q/? select option/text/reject/withdraw/skip/quit/help. Prompt Action [d=option, t=text, r=reject, w=withdraw, s=skip, q=quit, ?=help]: ; d prompts Option label: ; t prompts Decision text: ; writes prompt Rationale: . Unknown labels and blank fields re-prompt that field; other action input re-prompts action. Summary: N decided, N rejected, N withdrawn, N skipped, N failed. Counts cover visited outcomes only; quit/EOF do not count remaining records. EOF discards an incomplete answer; input read errors exit 1. Failed commands report stderr, advance to next question, and cause exit 1. Keep typed text and rationale, trim option labels as decide does. These line-mode choices keep scripts simple and preserve one-shot command behavior.

**Not in this slice:** a full-screen TUI or curses; HTML output; a web server (C09); -i with --all (cross-repo deciding) or with --json; amend or supersede from the walk; any change to what decide/reject/withdraw validate.

## Why

Listed in the Later tier to speed up batch answering. Owner decisions 2026-10-18: a line-mode TUI, invoked as adj inbox -i (not a new command), standard library only (bufio on stdin, no terminal raw mode), owner-only like decide: the agent snippet must not suggest it. For each open record, oldest first as adj inbox orders them: print the record as adj inbox does, then prompt for an action: decide by option label, decide with free text, reject, withdraw, skip, quit; decide/reject/withdraw then prompt for the rationale (--why), required and not blank. Writes go through commands.Decide / Reject / Withdraw so validation, history and decided_by ($ADJ_DECIDED_BY, or --by) are the same as the one-shot commands.

## Failing tests

Red first, scripted stdin, stores in t.TempDir():
- Two open records; script 'decide label a' + rationale for the first and 'skip' for the second: the first is decided with decision a, rationale as typed, decided_by from --by or ADJ_DECIDED_BY, one decide history entry; the second stays open; exit 0.
- Free-text decide, reject and withdraw each move the record as the one-shot commands would (compare the resulting record with one made by adj decide/reject/withdraw on a copy).
- An unknown option label or a blank rationale re-prompts (does not write, does not abort the walk).
- quit stops at once and leaves the rest open; EOF on stdin behaves as quit (exit 0, nothing half-written).
- A record that changed status under the walk (decided by another process between display and write) reports the error from commands.Decide on stderr and continues (exit 1 at the end, or as C32 decides).
- Empty inbox: prints nothing, exit 0.
- -i --json, -i --all and -i with an argument exit 2.
- Prompts and summary line (e.g. '2 decided, 1 rejected, 3 skipped') are pinned by a golden test.
